key_insight: The paper introduces a reasoning-focused benchmark and LLM workflow to verify whether clinical notes and structured EHR tables truly agree, beyond simple value matching.
clinical_relevance: Improving note-table consistency checks could help catch documentation mismatches that affect patient safety, chart quality, and downstream clinical decisions.
method: Built EHR-ReasonCon from MIMIC-III with expert-guided labels for 8,048 note-derived entities.
Created EHR-Inspector to segment notes, identify anchor entities and time references, and compare them against tables using exploration tools.
Evaluated results with expert-validated LLM-as-a-judge under both harsh and lenient criteria.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports high-quality ground-truth annotations and state-of-the-art performance across multiple backbones on the new benchmark.
watch_item: Performance depends on specialized annotation and table-exploration tooling, so real-world deployment may require careful validation across different EHR systems and documentation styles.
paper_title: Towards Error-Free EHRs: Reasoning-Intensive Consistency Verification Between Clinical Notes and Structured Tables in Electronic Health Records
